item.title: Mynah 0.2.3-beta.1
item.description:
**Beta: not the stable release.** This build makes dictation work in **remote desktops and VMs that block copy and paste**, and fixes a freeze.
### New in beta 1 - **Type instead of paste.** In apps where the clipboard doesn't reach (Windows App, out of the box), Mynah types what you dictated key by key instead of pasting it. Add other remote desktop or VM apps in **Settings › Type instead of paste › Add app…**, or remove one by clicking its ✕. - **Fixed a freeze** where Mynah stopped responding (often noticed only at the next dictation) while it re-registered for audio changes from every app on the Mac, over and over. - **Mynah keeps its own log** at `~/Library/Logs/Mynah/app.log`, next to `engine.log`. If Mynah stops responding for more than 5 seconds, it notes it there and saves a `hang-*.txt` snapshot next to it. Send those along when reporting a freeze; no admin account needed.
### What to try - Dictate into a Windows session in Windows App, including punctuation like `?`, `!`, `:` and quotes. - Switch to another app while a long dictation is being typed: typing stops.
### Known limitations - Typing is slower than pasting: a long dictation takes a few seconds to appear. - Emoji and characters that need Option or a dead key (é, ü, …) may not come through in a remote session. - Command mode can't read the selected text inside a VM that blocks the clipboard. - Updating a beta resets macOS permissions, because builds are ad-hoc signed.
### Install Download **Mynah-*.dmg** below, drag **Mynah** into **Applications**, open it, and use **System Settings › Privacy & Security › Open Anyway** the first time. Already on a beta? Mynah offers this update itself. On the stable channel, turn on **Settings › Updates › Beta versions** or install by hand. Requires Apple Silicon and macOS 14.2 or later for meeting capture.

item.title: Mynah 0.2.2
item.description:
Private, on-device dictation for Apple Silicon Macs. Hold **Fn**, talk, let go — clean text appears wherever you're typing.
### New in 0.2.2 **Faster dictation** - **No more 2–3 second waits after Mynah sits idle.** The speech and cleanup models now stay ready in memory between dictations, and Mynah wakes them up as soon as you press the hotkey, while you're still talking. The first dictation after a short sleep dropped from about 3.2 s to 0.6 s in testing. (Macs with 24 GB or more keep the models in memory; smaller Macs rely on the wake-up alone.)
**Speaker recognition in meetings** - Mynah tells apart the other people on a call and learns their voices. After a call, the meeting page shows a **Speakers** card: name **Speaker 1**, **Speaker 2**, … once, and later meetings label them automatically. The notes and to-dos use their names too ("Bob will send the deck"). - Name people from the Speakers card or by clicking a name chip in the transcript. **Write notes again** refreshes the notes after a rename, and **⋯ › Find speakers** works on older meetings whose audio is still saved. - Turn it off in **Settings › Meetings › Recognize speakers**. **People…** lets you rename or delete people, or forget all voices. Voices and names stay on your Mac.
**Dictation** - **Music and videos pause while you dictate** and resume when you stop (Spotify, Music, Podcasts, YouTube and other browser media, most video players). Turn it off in **Settings › Pause media while dictating**. - **Sleep and screen lock are handled:** a dictation left running is cancelled quietly, and the hotkey no longer gets stuck after waking.
**Meetings** - **Sharing your screen no longer ends the recording**, and going straight from one named meeting into the next starts a new recording. - **Teams mute detection works on a fresh Teams** and recognizes more versions of the mic button. If Mynah can't tell whether you're muted, it notifies you instead of quietly recording. - **Fewer "You" lines from other people on speakers,** including short "yeah" / "okay" lines your mic picked up from the call. - **A recording ends when your Mac sleeps** instead of filling up with silence, and call detection restarts on wake. The meeting mic recovers if it fails to reopen.
**App** - **Better battery life:** windows no longer redraw while you're not using them. - **Fewer freezes**, a sidebar that opens pages from the start, windows that keep focus after dialogs and reopen where you left them (or back on screen if that display is gone), and confirmations before deleting audio, forgetting a person, or quitting mid-recording. - Builds are ad-hoc signed, so macOS asks for Microphone and Accessibility again after each update.
### Install 1. Download **Mynah-*.dmg** below, open it, and drag **Mynah** into **Applications**. 2. Open Mynah. macOS will say it can't verify the developer (Mynah isn't notarized by Apple yet). Click **Done**, then go to **System Settings › Privacy & Security**, scroll down, and click **Open Anyway** next to Mynah. You only do this once. 3. Follow the setup window: allow Microphone and Accessibility, and let it download the models (~9 GB, one time).
**Requirements:** Apple Silicon (M1 or later), macOS 14+ (14.2+ for meeting capture), 16 GB RAM recommended (8 GB works with the smaller cleanup model), ~12 GB free disk.
See the [README](https://github.com/lukekerwin/mynah#readme) for details. Verify the download with the `.sha256` file if you like.

item.title: Mynah 0.2.2-beta.10
item.description:
**Beta: not the stable release.** This build adds **speaker recognition** to meeting capture: Mynah tells apart the other people on a call and learns their voices, so after you name someone once, later meetings label them automatically. Voices and names stay on your Mac.
### New in beta 10 - **Music and videos pause while you dictate** and pick up where they left off when you stop (Spotify, Music, Podcasts, YouTube and other browser media, most video players). Only what Mynah paused is resumed. Turn it off in **Settings › Pause media while dictating**.
### New in beta 9 - **Better battery life.** Mynah's windows no longer redraw every few seconds while you're not using them, and the menu no longer reloads every meeting each second during a call.
### New in beta 8 - **The sidebar opens pages from the start.** Clicking Meetings shows the list, not the last meeting you opened. Pages open at the top. - **The live transcript's Close button closes it** instead of popping right back open. - **Mynah asks before** deleting a meeting's audio, forgetting a person, or quitting while a call is being recorded. - **Due dates read naturally** ("Tomorrow", "Mon, Oct 20"), with overdue ones in coral. - **Esc** cancels the meeting setup and Edit to-do. **The window reopens where you left it.**
### New in beta 7 - **Mynah's window keeps focus** when you close a popover or dialog (like New to-do), instead of dropping behind other apps. - **Fewer freezes:** the meeting page no longer reloads the whole meeting every second during a call, Mynah gives up quickly on a busy app (Teams mid-call) when you dictate, and quitting can't hang on the engine.
### New in beta 6 - **Going straight from one meeting into the next starts a new recording** instead of carrying the first one on (needs a meeting with a name; ad hoc calls can't be told apart yet).
### New in beta 5 - **Sharing your screen no longer ends the recording.** Mynah took Teams hiding the call window while you present as you leaving the call.
### New in beta 4 - Leaving a Teams call no longer sends a false "can't see Teams' mute button" warning. - Debug menu only: **Watch Teams participants** records how Teams' participant tiles change during a call, to explore naming speakers from who Teams shows as talking.
### New in beta 3 - **Teams mute detection works on a fresh Teams.** Mynah couldn't read Teams' call window unless something else had already made it readable, so being muted was never noticed and leaving the call didn't end the recording. Both work now.
### New in beta 2 - **Fewer "You" lines from other people on speakers.** Mynah is much stricter about what counts as you talking over the call, and it measures the speaker leak steadily across the whole meeting. - **Short "yeah" / "okay" lines** your mic picked up from the call are now hidden too. - **Teams mute detection** recognizes more versions of the mic button. If Mynah still can't see whether you're muted, it now sends a notification instead of quietly recording your mic.
### What to try - Record a Teams call with two or more other people. When it's processed, the meeting page shows a **Speakers** card: anyone Mynah doesn't know yet is **Speaker 1**, **Speaker 2**, … - Name them from the Speakers card, or click a name chip in the transcript. Pick someone you've named before, or **New person…**. **Clear name** undoes a wrong name. - In the next call with the same people, they should be named automatically. The notes and to-dos use their names too ("Bob will send the deck"). - Renamed someone after the notes were written? Use **Write notes again** on the Speakers card. - Older meetings whose audio is still saved: **⋯ › Find speakers**. - **Settings › Meetings › Recognize speakers** turns it off. **People…** lets you rename or delete people, or forget all voices.
### Known limitations - The first time, Mynah downloads a 21 MB voice model. - Your own mic is still always **You**. Only the call audio is split by speaker. - People who talk for less than about 5 seconds aren't remembered. - Several people in one room on one mic, or someone who joins from a different mic or headset than usual, may come up as a new Speaker. Name them again and Mynah learns that voice too. - Updating a beta resets macOS permissions, because builds are ad-hoc signed.
### Install Download **Mynah-*.dmg** below, drag **Mynah** into **Applications**, open it, and use **System Settings › Privacy & Security › Open Anyway** the first time. Already on a beta? Mynah offers this update itself. On the stable channel, turn on **Settings › Updates › Beta versions** or install by hand. Requires Apple Silicon and macOS 14.2 or later for meeting capture.

### New in beta 3 - **Teams mute detection works on a fresh Teams.** Mynah couldn't read Teams' call window unless something else had already made it readable, so being muted was never noticed and leaving the call didn't end the recording. Both work now.
### New in beta 2 - **Fewer "You" lines from other people on speakers.** Mynah is much stricter about what counts as you talking over the call, and it measures the speaker leak steadily across the whole meeting. - **Short "yeah" / "okay" lines** your mic picked up from the call are now hidden too. - **Teams mute detection** recognizes more versions of the mic button. If Mynah still can't see whether you're muted, it now sends a notification instead of quietly recording your mic.
### What to try - Record a Teams call with two or more other people. When it's processed, the meeting page shows a **Speakers** card: anyone Mynah doesn't know yet is **Speaker 1**, **Speaker 2**, … - Name them from the Speakers card, or click a name chip in the transcript. Pick someone you've named before, or **New person…**. **Clear name** undoes a wrong name. - In the next call with the same people, they should be named automatically. The notes and to-dos use their names too ("Bob will send the deck"). - Renamed someone after the notes were written? Use **Write notes again** on the Speakers card. - Older meetings whose audio is still saved: **⋯ › Find speakers**. - **Settings › Meetings › Recognize speakers** turns it off. **People…** lets you rename or delete people, or forget all voices.
### Known limitations - The first time, Mynah downloads a 21 MB voice model. - Your own mic is still always **You**. Only the call audio is split by speaker. - People who talk for less than about 5 seconds aren't remembered. - Several people in one room on one mic, or someone who joins from a different mic or headset than usual, may come up as a new Speaker. Name them again and Mynah learns that voice too. - Updating a beta resets macOS permissions, because builds are ad-hoc signed.
### Install Download **Mynah-*.dmg** below, drag **Mynah** into **Applications**, open it, and use **System Settings › Privacy & Security › Open Anyway** the first time. Already on a beta? Mynah offers this update itself. On the stable channel, turn on **Settings › Updates › Beta versions** or install by hand. Requires Apple Silicon and macOS 14.2 or later for meeting capture.

item.title: Mynah 0.2.1
item.description:
Private, on-device dictation for Apple Silicon Macs. Hold **Fn**, talk, let go — clean text appears wherever you're typing.
### New in 0.2.1 Meeting capture fixes: - **No more "You" lines from other people on speakers.** Call audio your mic picks up through the speakers is removed before transcription, and echoed lines disappear from the live transcript as you go. - **Muted in Teams is detected more reliably**, and the live transcript tells you when Mynah can't see Teams' mute button. - **Recordings end when the call does.** Mynah now notices when you leave a Teams call instead of recording until you stop it. - **Meeting titles describe the call** (e.g. "Q3 budget review with finance") instead of "Teams call" and the date, unless Teams gave the meeting a name or you renamed it. - **Readable transcripts:** what the other people say is split into paragraphs at pauses instead of one long block. - Builds are ad-hoc signed, so macOS asks for Microphone and Accessibility again after each update.
### Install 1. Download **Mynah-*.dmg** below, open it, and drag **Mynah** into **Applications**. 2. Open Mynah. macOS will say it can't verify the developer (Mynah isn't notarized by Apple yet). Click **Done**, then go to **System Settings › Privacy & Security**, scroll down, and click **Open Anyway** next to Mynah. You only do this once. 3. Follow the setup window: allow Microphone and Accessibility, and let it download the models (~9 GB, one time).
**Requirements:** Apple Silicon (M1 or later), macOS 14+, 16 GB RAM recommended (8 GB works with the smaller cleanup model), ~12 GB free disk.
See the [README](https://github.com/lukekerwin/mynah#readme) for details. Verify the download with the `.sha256` file if you like.

item.description:
